tagline: Thirty-two flat miles of savannah, kept open by fire.
intro: Nine miles south of Bristol, SR 12 enters the Apalachicola National Forest. The byway follows it almost four miles, turns onto SR 379, passes through Sumatra and takes SR 65 south to the forest's southern tip, 32 miles over flat to gently rolling ground. Much of it crosses savannah, open grassland under scattered longleaf pine that often holds water the year round.

In the wiregrass grow pitcher plants and sundews, wild orchids and blazing star, with bays of magnolia and cypress between. The open pine country stays open by burning, and open ground of that kind is what the endangered red-cockaded woodpecker favors.

moments.title: Sumatra
moments.text: A community of 148 on SR 65, with the Apalachicola Northern rails running alongside the highway through the forest.

moments.title: Prospect Bluff Historic Sites
moments.text: On a 12-foot bluff over the Apalachicola, six miles from Sumatra, lie the ruins of a British fort of 1814 and of Fort Gadsden, built inside its walls in 1818.
